summary: Dependency-confusion beacon in @greenlake/common-context posts host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package self-describes as a 'Compatibility shim' and exports an inert Proxy that returns no-op functions for every property, providing no functional API. Its only runtime behavior is a beacon in beacon.cjs that fires both from the npm postinstall lifecycle hook and on require() via index.js. The beacon collects the installer's OS hostname, __dirname install path, and process.cwd() (which commonly embed the Unix username and internal project/repo names) along with Node version, and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded plaintext bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc with an x-beacon-package header identifying the resolving package. The scoped name @greenlake/* mimicking an internal namespace, the inert public API, and the automatic callback to a hardcoded bare-IP operator on install and import together match the shape of a dependency-confusion probe: resolving this package on an installer's machine silently discloses internal host, user, path, and namespace information to an external operator the installer did not opt into.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
